proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed a two-visit full-reference recurrent-rate information bound, a tangent-realization argument, an analytic strict-variance witness, and a conditional cross-fitted estimator. D0.5 capped the delivered contribution at subfield because its projected paper score was 6.8, below the field threshold of 7.4, with no bounded in-scope salvage. The math and rubric panels returned revise before the novelty triage stopped the run; their findings remain unrepaired, so this archive does not certify mathematical soundness.
tldr: Current and lagged recurrent-admission rate blips are linked to the law-indexed parameter \(P\mapsto\beta(P)\), the unique root of a two-visit full-reference observed-law restriction system. Its causal construction uses an early potential risk-set mean-rate contrast and a late natural-policy full-reference blip-down equality, while the benchmark is distinct from the published successive-blip SNCURE model; no containment in either direction is claimed. A backward conditional-value correction, coercive continuum covariance equation, and realized union-model tangent graph yield the joint canonical gradient and sharp \(2\times2\) bound. The bound is attained by a fully data-measurable nested cross-fitted Galerkin--Newton estimator: a deterministic reference basis is converted with Laplace-smoothed empirical baseline Gram matrices, each fitted gradient contains exactly one centered reward plus one death-martingale augmentation, and deterministic rate-based spectral flooring and truncation replace oracle clipping. The resulting covariance estimate gives joint Wald coverage under the displayed aggregate nuisance rates; unrestricted full-history learning remains open.
